title: Rule evaluation order and the classic mistakes

videos.script: A rule set is read from the top, and the first rule that matches decides. Everything below it is never asked. {{first}} That one fact explains most firewall mistakes, and this lesson makes four of them on purpose. A quarantine that quarantines nothing. A /16 typed where a /24 was meant, which opens SSH to the staff LAN. A rule written the wrong way round, which no packet can ever match. And a rule added after the end. {{four}} Each one loads without a complaint. Each one shows itself in the same place: a counter that stays at zero, or a test that tries the traffic. {{counters}} Last, that test, written down and run after every change. {{test}}
